content.value_statement: Metabase contributors need consistent TypeScript and JavaScript standards during feature work. This skill guides strict typing, reusable patterns, and verification steps for safer changes.
actual_capabilities: Guides new TypeScript and JavaScript code away from any and unsafe casts.
Promotes existing Metabase API types, domain IDs, and derived type helpers.
Recommends discriminated unions and exhaustive handling for variant state.
Encourages boundary typing with unknown, guards, and narrow internal contracts.
Provides structure guidance for helpers, components, naming, and comments.
Reminds users to inspect inferred types and run project type checks.
limitations: It is specialized for Metabase frontend conventions and may not fit other projects.
It does not run type checks or language server actions by itself.
It references shared guidance files that are not included in this audited bundle.
It gives coding standards, not complete feature requirements or product decisions.

use_cases.title: Implement Typed Features
use_cases.description: Use the skill while adding TypeScript or TSX code that must follow project typing rules.

use_cases.title: Refactor JavaScript Safely
use_cases.description: Use the skill to plan a conversion path with boundary types, guards, and smaller helpers.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Use the skill to spot unsafe casts, weak null handling, duplicated types, and missing verification.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Metabase Type Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply this skill while adding a small TypeScript component. Avoid any, reuse existing Metabase types, and list verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this JavaScript change toward TypeScript. Identify boundary types, guards, and smaller helpers before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Model Feature State
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a type model for this feature state. Use discriminated unions, narrow nullability, and exhaustive handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this planned Metabase frontend change for type safety, reusable domain types, null handling, naming, component extraction, and final type-check commands.

output_examples.input: Add a typed loading state for a Metabase frontend view.
output_examples.output: The response describes a discriminated state model, existing API types to reuse, and verification with project type checks.

output_examples.input: Review a refactor that removes a loose cast from a data boundary.
output_examples.output: The review flags the unsafe cast, suggests a boundary type guard, and asks for focused helper extraction.

output_examples.input: Convert a small JavaScript utility before adding new behavior.
output_examples.output: The response proposes a separate TypeScript conversion step, narrow input types, and a follow-up implementation plan.

best_practices: Check existing Metabase API and domain types before adding new types.
Use unknown with guards for boundary data, then keep internal code narrow.
Run the project type check after TypeScript or TSX edits.
anti_patterns: Introducing any, as any, or broad casts to quiet compiler errors.
Duplicating generated API types instead of deriving from existing definitions.
Threading nullable values through many layers without narrowing at the source.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete Metabase features?
faq.answer: It guides implementation quality, but it does not define product requirements or own the full feature design.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Metabase?
faq.answer: You can reuse general TypeScript advice, but many recommendations assume Metabase project structure and types.

faq.question: Does it allow any in tests or prototypes?
faq.answer: The skill says new code must not introduce any, explicit or implicit.

faq.question: What should I do with untyped external data?
faq.answer: Type it at the boundary with a declared type, unknown with guards, or a small typed wrapper.

faq.question: Does it replace a TypeScript compiler check?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly asks users to inspect inferred types and run the project type check.

faq.question: Why is this audit not fully safe?
faq.answer: The skill references parent shared files that are not present in the audited bundle.
